work_or_context: Gabriel Daniel, Histoire de France depuis l’établissement de la monarchie françoise dans les Gaules, tome I
clio_action: presents/dedicates the book to the French Monarchy
analytic_function: Clio mediates between historical writing and monarchy; history presented as a gift/act of dynastic service
notes: Utpictura18 explicitly identifies Clio and describes the scene as an allegorical dedication by Clio to the French Monarchy. François Verdier design; Charles-Louis Simonneau engraving.

work_or_context: Isaac de Larrey, Histoire d'Angleterre, vol. III or IV
clio_status: generic History; do not relabel as Clio
clio_action: History and a Spirit write the history of England
analytic_function: negative-control case: a female History personification can perform Clio-like work without being catalogued as Clio
notes: British Museum calls the figure History, not Clio. Time tries to devour books while spirits rescue them; Fame carries Larrey's portrait. Keep this distinction hard.

publisher_or_institution: Andries van Damme / serial publication context
clio_status: explicit Clio in Groningen interpretation; contemporary explanation calls her Historie-schryfster
clio_action: paints/writes the portrait-history of Cardinal Alberoni but is stopped before finishing
companions_or_counterforces: Fama/Pheme stops her; Curiosity; Mercury; Christmas Flood
historical_object: current European events, especially Alberoni's expansion policy
analytic_function: Clio as provisional contemporary historian: Fame blocks premature closure because the event's outcome is not yet known
notes: University of Groningen identifies Clio explicitly. Joop Koopmans's transcription of the contemporary explanatory poem calls her 'Historie-schryfster' and says Fama prevents her from completing Alberoni's image until events clarify.

work_or_context: Paul de Rapin de Thoyras, Histoire d'Angleterre, tome I
companions_or_counterforces: Time; winged Spirits; first inhabitants of Britain
historical_object: long-duration English history from ancient inhabitants through rulers
analytic_function: Clio organizes historical succession against Time/oblivion; the frontispiece spatializes chronology
notes: British Museum: François Morellon de la Cave, 1723; 'Clio ... writing a history of England' with Time and six ruler medallions. Publication vol. I is 1724.

work_or_context: Catharine Macaulay, The History of England from the Revolution to the Present Time
publisher_or_institution: R. Cruttwell; E. & C. Dilly; T. Cadell; J. Walter
clio_status: Clio identification is scholarly/iconographic, not an inscribed label on the print
clio_action: historian writes while embodying Clio and Liberty
attributes: quill; five volumes of her History; republican Roman dress; political inscription
companions_or_counterforces: Liberty/republican iconography; Dr Wilson as addressee
historical_object: post-Revolution English history and the historian's own political authority
analytic_function: historian and muse collapse into one body: Clio moves from external guarantor of history to the historian's self-fashioning
notes: Natalie Zemon Davis explicitly reads the 1778 frontispiece as Macaulay simultaneously Clio, Liberty, and herself. NPG confirms the Robert Edge Pine composition and James Caldwall engraving tradition used in 1778.

object_role: iconographic control; not yet tied to a historiographical frontispiece
analytic_function: control for pedagogical Clio: history transmitted through reading and instruction rather than dynastic dedication or event narration
notes: Rijksmuseum explicitly describes seated Clio, muse of history, instructing putti who study books.

work_or_context: Clio, Almanach iconologique: Les muses, vol. VI
clio_action: appears as named muse of history
attributes: book inscribed 'Tucidedes'; other attributes to verify visually

notes: National Gallery of Art: engraved by Emmanuel Jean Nepomucène de Ghendt after Hubert François Gravelot, published 1769; plate inscription includes 'Tucidedes' and 'CLIO'.
